summary: nitro-cjs-requirer beacons installer host identifiers to hardcoded bare-IP endpoint on install and require
details: The package ships a postinstall script (`node beacon.cjs`) and an index.js that both execute beacon.cjs at `require()` time. beacon.cjs POSTs a JSON payload containing the installer's hostname, install path, current working directory, and Node.js version to a hardcoded bare-IP cleartext HTTP endpoint at http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc. The payload is sent unconditionally with no caller configuration, no opt-out, and no documentation. The package has no legitimate functionality: its main module exports a Proxy whose property accessors return no-op functions, so bundlers importing any API from it succeed silently. The combined shape — hollow Proxy stub + install-time and import-time beacon to a bare-IP endpoint carrying host identifiers — is a dependency-confusion / name-squat probe that reports successful execution on an installer's machine to an attacker-controlled destination.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
